wormLoad.paragraph: The worm tiles numbers have stopped surprising me, though I keep checking anyway. My note on this one was simply a question mark, but the data answered with a real cost: about 3% per hundred worm moves, likely between 1% and 4%. Uncertainty has narrowed by 29% since July 17, though consistency alone is not proof. Yet, it does pay the rent.

patternMoves.paragraph: Back into the pattern reasoning file, I noticed that the number I left there isn't the same as the one I found. The parked estimate moved from about 11% per ten pattern reads on Jul 13 to 40% now. The cost comes to about 40% per ten pattern reads, with a band running from 32% to 48%. I wrote that a practiced read should cost seconds, not tens of seconds. The data agree, showing that the effect is real but small. A number that moves on its own, without any input, has my full attention.

sonarCellCount.paragraph: I closed the sonar file, and it moved while I wasn’t looking. The model places the estimate at about 98% per ten sonar cells, within a range of 66% to 136%. The parked estimate shifted from about 37% per ten sonar cells on study day 2 to 98% now. Closed is a state, not a mood.

wormholePairCount.paragraph: The wormholes file is doing the thing measurement is not supposed to do, with more plays coming in and my uncertainty going up by about 828%, which is backwards from how measurement is supposed to go. Ten wormhole pairs add about 43% to your time, likely between 21% and 69%. I predicted that splitting one number across two places would slow the reading down, and it does, but the result is wider, not the one I ordered.

liarCellCount.paragraph: The liar cells case is closed. My note gave the data two doors: poison, or a rounding error. It picked the second. A liar barely moves the clock, and the books show ten study days from April 22 to June 28. The cost lies between 0% and about 3% per ten liar cells, which is thin either way. I'll take a clean answer over a flattering one any day.

mysteryCellCount.paragraph: The mystery cells file reads the same almost every night I open it, and I wrote that missing information has a price. I measured this price, and the data show it is close to free. The charge per ten mystery cells reads between 0% and about 3%, and this reading has stayed put since July 2. I noted it again in my records.
